note: The base product's own country-word guard (fe-country-split-plan §4.8, §4.11 rule 6), read by lib/country-words.mjs: no file of fe/ or of the kit beside it, country-kit/…, names one of these words — an authority's name or host, a country's locale or place — unless an entry of `allowed` permits that word in that file, with its reason and, where the need ends, the phase that ends it (`until`). A word is matched case-insensitively as a literal substring of the NFC text and of each path, so a word inside a longer one counts. The guard covers every file git lists in fe/ and country-kit/, named as the zip names them (the kit's as country-kit/…), but this list (the tree mode, run by test:guards, which reports the words and every entry that permits nothing, so the list shrinks as the files lose the word) and every entry of the source zip (the zip mode, run by source-zip.mjs build and guard, the example harness and the publish workflow, which reports the words only, since an entry for a file outside the zip permits nothing there). An entry whose path is a glob permits its word in every file the glob matches, a new spec included: a reviewer of a new spec should know that it passes the guard without an entry of its own. Language names are not words: a language is a pack (R3), and the base product's specs use them as sample languages. This file stays out of the zip, because it names every word, and a country never runs the guard.
